document.title: Phase 5: XSD 1.1 validation and schema-aware typing
document.p: Goal (PLAN.md): XSD 1.1 schemas compiled from schema documents, trees validated against them into typed trees, and schema awareness in XPath, XQuery and XSLT (import schema, validate, xsl:import-schema, validation and type attributes, schema-element() tests); sxml validate (below). It starts alongside the end of Phase 4 () and must not regress the Phase 4 counts. Design: . Rules for parallel packets are those of docs/tasks/phase-2.md (, , : a packet starts when every packet in its "After" list is committed).

item.p: One public header, include/sxml/schema.h: an sxml_schema (lifecycle quintet) compiled from schema documents given as text, as parsed nodes or through the resource resolver (new kind SXML_RESOURCE_KIND_SCHEMA_DOCUMENT, processor.h); an sxml_schema_validator (quintet) that is a tree builder: it takes the events of the tree to validate and passes them on, annotated, to a result builder; sxml_schema_validate_node for an existing node; errors with XSD constraint names as codes and a report sink that receives all of them.

Validation is a tree builder filter. The XML parser feeds it while parsing (sxml validate, fn:doc with validation), the tree copier feeds it an existing node (XQuery validate, XSLT validation), node construction can feed it directly. The validated tree is an ordinary arena tree: the builder events already carry type annotation, is-id, is-idrefs and nilled (tree.h); defaults and normalized attribute values are just the events the validator sends. No new tree kind.

Typed values are derived, not stored: from the string value and the type annotation, in sxml_node_make_typed_value (src/xdm_node.c), for every tree without a get_typed_value operation (a contract comment in tree.h and xdm.h).

Types live in the one type registry. Schema compilation registers simple and complex type definitions through the internal sxml_type_registry_register_schema_type (src/types_internal.h): facets as text in the type description (types.h: sxml_facet), the content type of complex types (sxml_complex_type). Casting and facet checks are src/cast.c's, patterns the regex engine's XSD dialect (a flag, ). Schema types are found by name through their schema, not the registry (sxml_schema_find_type).

Schema components are internal (src/schema_internal.h, packet ), index-addressed in the schema's arena as the IR and ASTs are; the compile pipeline runs stages (read, resolve, simple types, complex types, identity constraints, assertions) that each live in their own file, so packets add files, not lines (the 2.0 pattern).
XPath is reused for assertions, type alternatives and identity constraints: compiled with the XPath API (xpath.h), evaluated by the one evaluator over subtrees the validator records.
Schema awareness in the languages replaces the one rejection point of each feature (): no parallel machinery, schema-element(N) is resolved statically into element tests.

section.title: sxml validate (design for 5.10; docs/CLI.md gets it when it works)
section.p: Validates each FILE (-: standard input) against the XSD 1.1 schema assembled from the SCHEMA documents. One intent (): it checks validity and writes no document; a typed result is the business of sxml xquery with validate.

row.cell: A schema document; repeatable, at least one. All of them, with every document they include, import, redefine or override (local files, relative to the referring document's path), form one schema
strict (default): each FILE's document element must have a global declaration; lax: one without is assessed laxly and is "not known"

item.p: The schema is compiled first. If it has errors, each goes to standard error as SCHEMA:LINE:COLUMN: CONSTRAINT: description (CONSTRAINT is the XSD constraint name, such as src-resolve) and no FILE is read.

Each FILE is parsed and validated in one pass (the parser feeds the validator; no tree is built). sxml prints nothing when every FILE is valid. Each error goes to standard error as FILE:LINE:COLUMN: CONSTRAINT: description, every error of the file, not only the first; a FILE that is not well-formed is reported as sxml check reports it. xsi:schemaLocation hints are ignored (5.16 added --use-schema-location, ).
Standard input is read at most once: - as a SCHEMA and a FILE, or twice, is a usage error.

With --format=json, one JSON object on standard output: {"schema":{"documents":["po.xsd"],"status":"valid"},"files":[{"file":"a.xml","status":"valid"},{"file":"b.xml","status":"invalid","errors":[{"code":"cvc-complex-type.2.4","line":3,"column":5,"byte_offset":40,"message":"..."}]}]}. The schema's status is valid, invalid (with errors as above, each with document), unreadable or failed; a FILE's is valid, invalid, not-known (lax), not-well-formed (with line, column, , message as for sxml check), unreadable or failed. Fields may be added later; existing ones do not change.

Exit status: 0 when every FILE is valid (or not known, with --mode=lax); 1 when the schema or a FILE is invalid or a FILE is not well-formed; 2 for a usage error (no --schema, no FILE, a bad --mode or --format, - twice); 3 when a SCHEMA or a FILE cannot be read (a document a SCHEMA includes that cannot be read is a schema error, src-include, exit 1); 4 at a limit. As for sxml check, 3 wins over 4 and 4 over 1.

section.pre: $ sxml validate --schema=po.xsd po.xml $ sxml validate --schema=po.xsd broken-po.xml broken-po.xml:7:5: cvc-complex-type.2.4: element 'comment' is not allowed here; expected 'shipTo' $ sxml validate --schema=po.xsd --format=json po.xml {"schema":{"documents":["po.xsd"],"status":"valid"},"files":[{"file":"po.xml","status":"valid"}]}
